title: Evidences that show chemical reaction has occurred
competency: Describe evidences that show a chemical reaction has occurred.

keywords.def: An insoluble solid formed when two solutions react.

en.text: Four signs show a chemical reaction: a colour change, a gas given off (bubbles), a temperature change, and a precipitate (a solid forming). Black copper oxide with sulfuric acid gives a blue solution. Magnesium in acid gives hydrogen bubbles.

screens.title: Fizz!
screens.ask: You add lemon juice to baking soda and it fizzes. What does the fizzing show?
screens.after: Bubbles mean a gas is given off. That is a sign of a chemical reaction.

screens.title: 3.3.2 Evidences
paras: In a chemical reaction, new products form.
A few signs show that a reaction has happened.

screens.title: 1. Colour changes
paras: Gently heat black copper oxide with sulfuric acid.
A blue solution of copper sulfate forms.
Copper oxide (black) + sulfuric acid → copper sulfate (blue) + water

screens.title: 2. A gas is given off
paras: Bubbles of hydrogen gas are given off.
Magnesium + hydrochloric acid → magnesium chloride + hydrogen

screens.title: 3. Temperature change
paras: Heat may be taken in or given out.
Potassium in water gives off hydrogen. So much heat forms that the gas burns.

screens.title: 4. A precipitate forms
paras: Mix silver nitrate and sodium chloride solutions.
An insoluble white solid forms. It is called a precipitate: silver chloride.
Silver nitrate + sodium chloride → silver chloride + sodium nitrate
